units.title: Readiness is a system
units.lesson: The RCUK primary dental care quality standard emphasizes risk assessment, trained staff, team preparation and access to appropriate resuscitation equipment. It is a UK professional standard, not an Indian legal rule. This foundation explains preparedness; it does not replace supervised skills training or provide a patient-treatment protocol.
units.question: Which is part of emergency preparedness?
choices: Trained staff and planned team roles
units.explanation: Preparedness includes people, planning and equipment.

units.title: Expand the structured vocabulary
units.lesson: In the 2025 RCUK first-aid guidance, ABCDE names Airway, Breathing, Circulation, Disability and Exposure. The sequence organizes assessment domains. Remembering the expansion is academic knowledge; it is not proof that a learner can assess or manage an emergency. Actual care requires appropriate training and local emergency systems.
units.question: What does B stand for in the ABCDE assessment framework?
rationales: Bleeding is relevant to care but is not this expansion.
This is not the B expansion.

units.title: Do not require skin signs in every severe reaction
units.lesson: RCUK 2025 describes anaphylaxis as involving airway, breathing or circulation problems, with or without skin or mucosal changes. Therefore an academic definition that requires a rash in every case is too narrow. This chapter teaches the limitation of that statement; no drug doses, self-treatment steps or diagnostic algorithm are supplied.
units.question: Which statement is too narrow?
choices: Airway or circulation problems can be relevant
Anaphylaxis always requires a visible rash
units.explanation: Skin or mucosal changes need not occur in every case.
rationales: This is compatible with the guidance.
The word always makes this false.

units.title: Keep breathing and circulation distinct
units.lesson: Ventilation concerns air movement into and out of the lungs. Circulation concerns blood movement through vessels. Both contribute to physiological function, but one observation does not measure every component of the other. Distinguish the terms in a viva before discussing more detailed emergency physiology. No patient threshold or treatment decision follows from this vocabulary alone.
units.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes the processes?
choices: Ventilation moves air; circulation moves blood
Both mean exactly the same measurement
units.explanation: Airflow and blood flow are different processes.
